title.narrative: Spotlight on pharmaceutical companies’ actions in women’s health and SRHR

description.narrative: Ahead of a special report in the 2022 Access to Medicine Index, the Foundation has published a Briefing on key issues in women's health and SRHR (sexual and reproductive health and rights), and the role of pharmaceutical companies in making sure essential health products are available and accessible to women in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).

title.narrative: Investor Action on Antimicrobial Resistance progress report

description.narrative: As part of World Antimicrobial Awareness Week 2022, the Investor Action on Antimicrobial Resistance has today published its first progress report. The report highlights the types of efforts investors have so far undertaken, and can undertake in future, to help turn the tide on rising antimicrobial resistance (AMR) – an urgent public health challenge.

description.narrative: On 9 April 2024, the Access to Medicine Foundation’s will convene an Amsterdam Session focusing on diabetes care. This event follows on from two previous events hosted by the Foundation's Diabetes Care Programme in 2022 and 2023, both of which were solutions-focused forums for discussion and information sharing.

description.narrative: The antibiotic market is unstable, with fragile supply chains and tough market conditions. This report sets out how these factors limit the development of a robust go-to-market model for such products. It features six case studies where companies and their partners are using a combination of access strategies to cut through the complexity and address access at a local level.

Expert panel discussion: Slowing the spread of superbugs, speeding up development and access

description.narrative: On Tuesday 28 June 2022, the Access to Medicine Foundation hosted an expert panel discussion in collaboration with Global Antibiotic Research and Development Partnership (GARDP). The event linked Dutch, European and global initiatives that address antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in order to reduce cross-border health security risks. High-level speakers shared their perspectives and research on the spread of AMR.

Writing and publishing the 2022 ATM Index

description.narrative: The 2022 Access to Medicine Index finds that since the COVID-19 pandemic hit, more pharmaceutical companies have stepped up to make some of their products more widely accessible in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). If the pandemic is to be a turning point in the fight for equitable access to medicine, companies must now scale their efforts to cover more products in their portfolios, and in a greater number of countries.
